title: An Engram admission deadline (deadline_exceeded) strands the queue: interrupted head isn't released by Resume and needs a manual cancel
outcome: An Engram admission that exceeds its budget never leaves a session silently stranded. The host reconciles the retained authorization automatically when it's safe (for example a head that is only a mailbox notification, whose content stays durable), and the operator's Resume either reconciles and continues or refuses with a stated reason and the exact next action.
acceptance: For a pure structured root mailbox-notification head with live, matching pre-Evaluate Bind-retry ownership, a nonfatal Bind Reconcile failure retains and automatically replays the exact original Bind request/key through the bounded recovery scheduler, without Resume, Cancel or a settings toggle. If reconciliation authorizes continuation, provider handoff occurs once; mailbox content remains durable and its cursor is not acknowledged by recovery. A deterministic test drives the actual admission failure and due ticks.

For a deadline-origin retained user/turn head, including one with no disable/re-enable history, Resume either makes durable progress through the existing exact reconciliation path or returns a typed non-2xx refusal naming the retained operation and supported next action. It never returns200 with the same interrupted, paused head and no durable progress. Tests cover the same-head post-drain race and distinguish a durably scheduled retry from provider delivery.

Tests preserve Unknown application identity, explicit Refuse/Defer, prepared or possibly-sent Begin, uncertain/active grant, real user/delegation content, local persistence uncertainty, Stop/operator pause, Cancel, successor replacement and changed authority. No content loss, duplicate provider handoff, fabricated NotStarted or blanket retry-code broadening is permitted. At bounded exhaustion the reason and next action remain visible; exact-input verification and independent acceptance establish the implemented cases.
